questions.subject: general_test
questions.stem: Arrange the following words in the order they would appear in a dictionary, from first to last: (A) Tiger (B) Tablet (C) Table (D) Tail (E) Tab. Choose the correct sequence from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Dictionary order compares letters from left to right. Tab comes before Table because it is a prefix of it, and Table comes before Tablet for the same reason. Tablet comes before Tail because b precedes i at the third letter, and Tail comes before Tiger because a precedes i at the second letter. The order is Tab, Table, Tablet, Tail, Tiger, which is (E), (C), (B), (D), (A).
questions.ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Ranking and order (alphabetical ordering)

questions.subject: general_test
questions.stem: Lata is taller than Mohan. Kiran is taller than Lata. Neha is shorter than Mohan but taller than Om. Arrange the following five persons from the tallest to the shortest: (A) Neha (B) Lata (C) Om (D) Kiran (E) Mohan. Choose the correct sequence from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Chain the comparisons: Kiran > Lata > Mohan from the first two clues, and Mohan > Neha > Om from the third. Combining the chains gives the full order Kiran, Lata, Mohan, Neha, Om, which is (D), (B), (E), (A), (C). Check a sequence against every clue, since one wrong adjacent pair rules it out.
questions.ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Ranking and order (height comparisons)

questions.subject: general_test
questions.stem: Five books (P), (Q), (R), (S) and (T) are placed on a shelf from left to right. S is at the left end. P is immediately to the right of R. Q is to the right of P but not next to P. Which arrangement from left to right is correct?
questions.explanation: S fixes the first place. R and P must then take two consecutive places among the second to the fifth, with P right after R. If P were in the fourth place, the only place to its right is the fifth, which is next to P, and if P were in the fifth place Q would have no place to its right. So R is in the second place and P in the third. Q must then be in the fifth place, to the right of P without touching it, which leaves T in the fourth place: S, R, P, T, Q.
questions.ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Seating and arrangement (linear, ordering by clues)

questions.subject: general_test
questions.stem: Statements: P > Q ≥ R; S < R; T ≥ P. Conclusions: (I) T > S. (II) S > Q. (III) P > R. Which conclusions follow?
questions.explanation: From T ≥ P > Q ≥ R > S, we get T > S (I follows) and P > R (III follows). From S < R ≤ Q we get S < Q, so S > Q does not follow (II).
questions.ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Inequality reasoning

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: How is the new position of a wavefront obtained from its previous position in Huygens' principle?

options.text: By joining the source to the point of observation with a straight line
As the surface on which all the rays meet at a single focus point
As the locus of points where the path difference at two slits is zero
As the envelope of secondary wavelets from points of the old wavefront

questions.explanation: Each point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets that spread out with the speed of the wave in the medium. The new wavefront is the forward envelope (common tangent surface) of these wavelets after a time t. This construction explains reflection and refraction of plane wavefronts.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.2 (Huygens' principle)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem:
Arrange the following electromagnetic waves in order of increasing wavelength, shortest wavelength first.
(A) Radio waves
(B) Visible light
(C) Gamma rays
(D) Microwaves
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Wavelength decreases as frequency increases across the spectrum. Radio waves are the longest, then microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are the shortest. So increasing wavelength runs gamma rays, visible light, microwaves, radio waves.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.4 (Electromagnetic spectrum)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem:
Match List-I (electromagnetic wave) with List-II (use).
List-I: (A) Infrared, (B) Ultraviolet, (C) X-rays, (D) Microwaves
List-II: (I) Sterilising water and killing bacteria, (II) Radiographs of bones, (III) Thermal imaging and TV remote controls, (IV) Radar and satellite communication
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Infrared is used in thermal imaging and remote controls (III), ultraviolet sterilises water and kills bacteria (I), X-rays produce radiographs of bones (II), and microwaves are used in radar and satellite communication (IV). The correct pairing is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.4 (Electromagnetic spectrum and uses)
